_comment: Special-request targets: sites crawled exclusively through the C3 (CamoFox) lane. No keyword gate — everything on the domain is kept, not just defence-relevant pages.

targets.name: sipri
targets._seed_note: Every top-level nav section is seeded directly. BFS from '/' alone reaches these eventually, but only after exhausting the shallow layers — on a ~10s/page C3 lane that is hours before a section is even touched. Seeding them makes coverage broad early instead of deep-and-narrow.
targets._rate_note: MEASURED 2026-07-21 against www.sipri.org (193.10.14.94, Apache): the host caps CONCURRENT connections per IP, it does not rate-limit. Same 10-request probe, only the crawl's own concurrency changed: with the crawl running at conc=4 the probe got 2/10 (80% ConnectError, ~15-20s each); with the crawl stopped, sequential got 8/10. Raising delay barely moves it (8s delay = 5/6), so the lever is CONCURRENCY, not spacing. conc=4 was self-defeating - the crawl's own 4 sockets ate the cap and refused its own pages, producing ZERO pages in 10 minutes. Hence conc=1. Do not raise this: a refused page costs a full 90s timeout plus retries, so parallelism here is strictly negative.
targets._sitemap_note: Phase 1: seed every published URL (57 sub-sitemaps). Phase 2: BFS from those pages finds anything the sitemap omits. Complete coverage without waiting for discovery to reach deep pages on a 15.5s-per-page origin.

targets.name: att_assistance
targets._seed_note: SIPRI's Arms Trade Treaty assistance mapping project ('Mapping ATT'). SIPRI content but a SEPARATE domain, so the sipri target can never reach it — the crawler is scoped to the seed's registered domain by design.
